slice: 2936-w6-captures-batch-3-widget (epic #2926, issue #2936 W6 part 2b, batch 3 — the third-party application)
note: THE CELLS OF THE THIRD-PARTY APPLICATION'S WIDGET, from REAL runs of the
blog-draft-writer agent started from INSIDE the widget by its own named-agent
start, on a host page served by another site, with the real model provider and
the real public MCP toolbox.
WHY THE ACTIONS ARE EMPTY, AND WHAT DRIVES THEM INSTEAD. The shipped `--walk`
CLI cannot bring a widget to any of these states, and this round measured that
rather than assuming it: the walk's chained frame selector DOES reach inside
the embed frame and DOES press the frame's own Sign in, but the frame's hosted
PKCE sign-in opens a SECOND WINDOW, which the closed action vocabulary has no
action for, and the credential it returns `lands in the ref and nowhere else`
(src/app/embed/assistant/embed-assistant-client.tsx) — so no fresh context can
carry one in either. The probe timed out on
`[data-embed-assistant][data-phase="active"]` after pressing Sign in. That
refusal is reported in README.md as a finding.
So the sequence driver `drivers/04-widget-run-sequence.mjs` drives the browser
— including the second window — and every record below is written by the
SHIPPED recorder on that live page: the shipped `playwrightPage` adapter, the
shipped `observeWalkCell` observer, the shipped `validateCaptureRecord` audit
tier and the shipped `mergeWalkRecords` merge. Nothing about a record is
supplied by this plan except the CLAIM it makes; every count, url, digest and
attribute in it is read off the live screen by the recorder.
export WALK_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:<port>
export SUPABASE_DB_URL=<the round's own database>
export HOST_PAGE_URL=<the third-party application's own origin>
ONE CLAIM IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS PLAN, AND WHY. A run started by the
widget's own named-agent start DOES reach `pending_approval` on this head and
the widget DOES draw `agent_hitl_screen` on `site_widget` — measured, and
photographed as a page control. The shipped plan validator refuses the cell:
`agent_hitl_screen` is recorded composition-only on this host, on the ground
that a widget conversation cannot start such a run. A plan the shipped
validator refuses is not a plan, so the claim stays out of it and the refusal
is reported as a FINDING in README.md, with the recorder driven for the same
claim so its own words are on the record too.
THE REVIEW CELLS ARE NOT IN THIS PLAN EITHER, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT.
A real widget-started run produced its artifact and its review gate went
PENDING in the database, and the widget's own column drew no review card at
all — on the live page and again after a reload. The code fact is in
README.md and in unreachable-cells.json; nothing is staged in its place.

steps.why: The widget's own conversation, with the run it started parked at the skills question: the chip-row held, in the palette the reader chose on the app's own control.

cells.requires: SECTION V of the ratified drawing at the contract's pin, verbatim: 'Where the assistant proposes the skills it means to use, the turn carries a chip-row: one chip per skill, each carrying its own Confirm, Adjust and Skip, so the reader shapes the run one skill at a time before it runs.' and 'The row is the whole card. There is no heading plate above it and no row-level submit beneath it — nothing states the question a second time, and nothing decides every skill at once. A skill is settled by pressing one of its own three affordances, and each chip then shows what it recorded.' With SECTION IX, verbatim: 'Every card appears on every host, and it is the same card wherever it appears: the same regions, the same states, the same data on screen, and the same actions its reader is authorized to take. Only the frame changes — the thread, the widget's panel, the run card's detail column, the gate region of the review page.'

steps.why: A schedule the person states in the widget's conversation BEFORE any run exists — the held carrier, first shown.

cells.requires: SECTION VI of the ratified drawing at the contract's pin, verbatim: 'The card is the scheduling step, in the turn — and it is the only thing drawn. Asked to run something later, the assistant reads the schedule out of the reader's own words and shows it back as the standard scheduling step: the question When should this run? over the three option rows, the chosen row taking the indigo edge and tint and owning its fields, and the estimated duration beneath.' 'There is no raw cron field: the schedule the reader stated is what the reader sees and confirms.' 'One card, five readings, and never a second card. The card is drawn once and stays where it is; what changes across its life is the floor beneath the rows and whether the rows still take a change. No summary box is ever drawn, no status label, and nothing stands between the reader and the form — the rows are the reading.' And the READING table's first row, verbatim: 'First shown — nothing exists yet | editable | Confirm'. And 'CONFIRM IS NEW HERE, AND ONLY HERE — AND THERE IS NO ADJUST'.
